transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Head of ML - Lynx), Tom Evans (VP Product - Lynx), Rashid Ahmed (SRE Lead - Lynx)

Summary (auto): quick QBR, usage up 28% q/q, cost concerns on high-throughput routes, a couple of reliability blips last month. Next: pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 + runbook, perf bench, pilot.

00:00 Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for making time, do we have everything on the calendar?
00:05 Priya: yea thanks Morgan, all good on our side, we wanted to focus on usage and cost first, then reliability incidents, and then roadmap stuff.
00:15 Morgan: perfect, quick nudge—we've pulled your token-level usage, I can walk through the trends real quick. Diego will jump into perf later.
00:30 Diego: hey, hi, quick note my audio is lagging a bit.
00:35 Tom: no worries, we can hear you.
00:45 Morgan: ok, starting usage slide — over the last quarter your overall call volume increased 28% driven by the recommendations route and the customer support assistant. Token spend is up 44% because the recs service has longer context windows and more regen calls.
01:10 Priya: that matches what we see, the recs model we've been running at 2k tokens average per session, and we started expanding personalized history retention in Feb which pushed tokens.
01:25 Morgan: noted. On a per-route basis the unit cost looks higher for the recs route; Diego, quick note on batching/caching options?
01:35 Diego: yeah so we spotted a couple things — continuous batching can help for the recs route but it depends on latency SLOs, and prefix/K-V cache is already on for the assistant but the recs pipeline isn't hitting the cache effectively because session keys are fairly unique. We can suggest conservative caching with a 30s TTL and adaptive batch windows. There's also a quantization profile we can test that preserves top-k outputs while cutting per-token GPU time.
02:05 Rashid: when you say K-V cache you mean the model KV cache? we've had some confusion internally about our eviction policies.
02:12 Diego: yeah, K-V as in key-value cache — sorry, sometimes the transcript auto hyphenates. eviction is important because you want hot prefixes to stay in GPU memory, but that does increase memory pressure.
02:28 Tom: cost is a major exec concern, if we can show a 20% unit cost reduction with little quality loss that's a win.
02:40 Morgan: agreed. We can run experiments on quantization + smarter batching. I'll put together expected unit cost delta and confidence intervals.
02:53 Priya: can you also show the tradeoff curve — latency vs cost — for the recs route? Our SLO is 150ms p95 for that route.
03:04 Diego: right; continuous batching will likely increase p95 for single-user requests unless we do predictive batching. For p95 150ms we might need a dedicated pool during peak.
03:16 Morgan: which leads to the dedicated vs hosted convo — Tom, where are you leaning?
03:22 Tom: we're trying to balance predictability with OpEx limits. Dedicated committed capacity with burst to hosted seems attractive but we need clear guarantees about latency and an easy failover to hosted.
03:36 Morgan: that's exactly our Redwood Dedicated offering — dedicated GPU pool with autoscaling and burst. We can tie SLA to the reserved capacity and have automated fallback to hosted if exhausted.
03:49 Priya: what's the onboarding time for private/VPC deploy if we wanted to evaluate on prem constraints?
03:56 Morgan: for private it's typically a few weeks for network setup, SOC2 docs etc depending on your security team's turnaround. For VPC peering + KMS integration usually 1–2 weeks if there are no tough firewall rules.
04:12 Rashid: our security team flagged SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs as blockers. also KMS/HSM integration for keys.
04:22 Morgan: we have SSO/SAML support, RBAC and token-level audit logs. KMS integration is supported, HSM is available for Private deployments, and we can share the SOC 2 type II report and architecture runbook.
04:36 Priya: ok please send the SOC2 and the runbook. can you include network diagrams and egress requirements?
04:42 Morgan: yes can do.
04:45 Tom: last month we had two brief reliability blips during peak — were those rate-limit related or infra related?
04:52 Diego: I looked into the traces — one was a transient autoscale lag due to a sticky inode inside the scheduler, the other was an unlucky model OOM during a spike caused by a regen storm. We've pushed a mitigation to limit regen fanout and improved backpressure on the request router.
05:15 Priya: thanks Diego, can you share the trace IDs? we want to map them to our internal incidents.
05:20 Diego: sure I'll post those in the follow-up.
05:25 Morgan: for the regen storm we recommended burst capacity rules and a queuing policy; that should reduce the probability of OOMs.
05:32 Tom: do you have example config for the queuing policy we could try?
05:37 Diego: yes, I'll include a recommended config with thresholds for the recs route.
05:42 Morgan: on the roadmap side — we discussed model rollouts and evals. Priya, you mentioned you want more regression alerts tied to your eval sets?
05:50 Priya: yes, our quality team needs alerts when a change to the model (even quantization) causes drift on the top-5 rec accuracy.
05:58 Morgan: we can wire up per-prompt evals and set regression thresholds; Redwood Optimize will track quality metrics and send alerts. Diego can help set up the eval harness.
06:08 Diego: we'll need the eval corpus and acceptance thresholds. also note evals run on a stable model snapshot to avoid noisy signals.
06:18 Priya: we'll share our eval set this week.
06:22 Tom: on pricing, can you walk through the new reserved capacity tiers and the pilot pricing?
06:27 Morgan: sure — for the pilot we'd propose a 2-week dedicated pool sized for your p95 requirements, with a temporary discount to make the bench realistic. After pilot we can recommend an annual reserved commit based on observed throughput, with clear burst to hosted terms. I'll send the spreadsheet.
06:45 Priya: what's the expected delta in unit cost if we move to a dedicated pool and enable quantization? ballpark.
06:53 Morgan: rough ballpark is 15–30% reduction depending on tail latency constraints and how much of your workload batches well. Diego will provide a more precise estimate after the bench.
07:05 Tom: ok good. for procurement, we need a statement of work and an initial PO if the pilot goes well — legal wants to see data handling clauses.
07:14 Morgan: we'll share our standard SOW and the data handling addendum. also I'll add the compliance attachments.
07:20 Rashid: also include specifics about log retention and ability to redact PII from logs.
07:26 Morgan: yes, log retention and redaction policies are part of the runbook doc we'll send.
07:32 Priya: timeline-wise, if we agree to pilot next week, can you get the perf bench in 2 weeks?
07:38 Diego: we can run the bench in 1–2 weeks depending on access to the test corpus and network access to staging.
07:45 Morgan: i'll coordinate with Rashid on network and creds.
07:49 Tom: action items recap?
07:52 Morgan: sure — Morgan to send pricing spreadsheet and SOW docs by Friday (2026-03-06); Diego to run perf benchmark and share trace IDs and recommended queuing config by 2026-03-12; Rashid to share staging VPC details and egress rules by 2026-03-08; Tom to confirm exec list by 2026-03-18.
08:20 Priya: sounds good, appreciate it.
08:25 Morgan: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive.
08:30 Tom: thanks everyone, bye.
08:33 End of recording.

Notes about transcript quality: some words auto-corrected (K-V vs KV, Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated), occasional speaker label flip.
